subject: Request: vulnerability ops runbook, on-call attestations and signed SLA note
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <security@acmepay.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmepay.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: VM evidence request + attestation for SOC2 review

Avery,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing for our SOC 2 vendor audit (Q3 intake) and need a compact evidence package showing Redwood's vulnerability management posture. Specifically can you provide the following by EOD Monday (6/1):

- Scan cadence by asset class (prod infra, control plane, third-party deps) and most recent full-scan export.
- Documented SLA / target remediation windows for Critical/High/Medium CVEs and the on-call escalation flow (who is notified, paging windows).
- A one-paragraph signed attestation on Redwood letterhead that you will notify Acme within 24 hours of any newly discovered Critical CVE affecting our fleet and provide an ETA for mitigation.
- Proof of recent remediation for CVE-2024-12345 (we saw a detection in our scans) — logs/snapshots or a screenshot of fix deployment.

We know some of this will reference internal runbooks — a redacted version is fine as long as it shows the cadence, owners, and escalation commitments. If you prefer we can accept a DocuSign-signed PDF for the attestation.

Appreciate a single ZIP or Drive folder link with the artifacts. If any of this needs to be routed to engineering/compliance at Redwood, please loop them in.

Regards,
Daniel Ruiz
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Payments

Attachments: none

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <security@acmepay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VM evidence request + attestation for SOC2 review

Daniel —

Thanks, we can produce everything you requested. Quick plan:

- Scan cadence + recent exports: we'll drop a full prod-scan CSV plus a weekly-digest for control-plane and third-party dependency scans into the Drive folder. Our scanner is Trivy for container images and Qualys for host-level coverage; cadence is: nightly image scan, weekly host scan, monthly dependency SBOM scan.

- SLA windows and on-call flow: brief doc below and an attestation PDF. High-level SLAs: Critical -> 24 hours triage and mitigation plan; High -> 72 hours acknowledgement and 7-14 day remediation target depending on exploitability; Medium -> scheduled in next available sprint (30-90 days). We maintain a 24/7 on-call rotation for infra on-call (Escalation: PagerDuty -> Eng Lead -> Security).

- CVE-2024-12345 proof: attaching a screenshot and the pipeline deployment notes for the hotpatch we applied on 2026-05-29.

We're preparing a single ZIP with: scan CSVs, the SLA+oncall runbook redaction, hotpatch notes, and a draft attestation PDF. Kimberly is on this thread to add technical artifacts; Marissa will coordinate delivery and DocuSign if you want signed attestation.

Action items:
- Kimberly: assemble scan exports + pipeline proof files and upload to Drive.
- Marissa: create DocuSign envelope for attestation and let Daniel know preferred signatory.

I'll follow up once the Drive link is ready (target: EOD Monday).

Best,
Avery Johnson
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hotpatch-notes-20260529.pdf (pipeline runbook excerpt), cve-2024-12345-remediation-proof.png

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, Daniel Ruiz <security@acmepay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 07:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VM evidence request + attestation for SOC2 review

Daniel / Avery —

Uploading the artifacts now to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/security/acme-vm-evidence-2026

What I uploaded:
- prod-full-scan-20260529.csv (Qualys host scan export)
- containers-trivy-20260529.csv (Trivy output for images)
- sbom-deps-20260501.csv (monthly dependency SBOM/CAIQ mapping)
- pipeline-deploy-20260529.log (CI/CD step showing hotpatch rollout)
- hotpatch-notes-20260529.pdf (change ticket + rollback instructions)
- cve-2024-12345-remediation-proof.png (container image ID + k8s rollout screenshot)

Technical summary (for auditors):
- Scanning: nightly image scans via Trivy integrated into CI; weekly host scans via Qualys; monthly SBOM and dependency checks against OSV and GHSA feeds. Findings are ingested into JIRA (SEC-XXXX board) and tagged by severity.
- SLA / remediation commitments: Critical (CVSS >= 9 or active exploit) -> 24-hour triage window, emergency patch/mitigation within 72 hours where possible; if immediate patch not available, compensating controls (WAF rules, network ACLs) are applied and tracked. High -> 72-hour acknowledgement, remediation within 7-14 days depending on risk; Medium -> triaged into backlog, remediation window up to 90 days.
- On-call/escalation: 24/7 infra on-call (PagerDuty) receives first alert; if no ACK in 15 minutes, escalates to Eng Lead; security ops is paged in parallel for critical findings. All pages generate an incident ticket with timeline.

CVE-2024-12345 note: this was a high-severity kernel CVE detected in a small subset of hosts. We rolled a kernel update and live-migrated workloads while the patch applied. The pipeline-deploy log and k8s rollout screenshot show the update completed 2026-05-29 22:03 UTC. No rollback recorded.

If you need a signed attestation, Marissa can package the one-paragraph statement on letterhead and trigger DocuSign.

- Kim

Attachments: prod-full-scan-20260529.csv (attached to Drive link), containers-trivy-20260529.csv

From: Daniel Ruiz <security@acmepay.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VM evidence request + attestation for SOC2 review

Avery / Kim —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. I reviewed the Drive folder and the kernel rollout evidence. That should satisfy our auditor's immediate asks. Two quick follow-ups:

1) Please proceed with the DocuSign attestation (we prefer a named signatory with role).
2) For the Critical SLA language we need explicit wording that Redwood will notify Acme within 24 hours of discovery "and" provide an initial mitigation ETA within 72 hours. Your note implies notification but phrases the mitigation window as "where possible" — auditors will want a definitive mitigation ETA clause. Can you include that exact phrasing in the attestation?

If you can send the signed PDF by EOD Tuesday we'll be able to include it in the SOC package.

Appreciate it —
Daniel
